commit.message:
docs: bring README, TESTING guide, and docs site up to date with the Bitcoin bridge

The BTC bridge (auto-deposit, self-registration watcher, real WrappedBTC
minting) had zero documentation anywhere despite being fully built and
live-verified. Adds it across the root README (architecture diagram,
module tables, a new Bitcoin bridge section), TESTING.md, contract/
README and circuits docs, and a new /concepts/bitcoin-bridge docs page —
including the honest disclosure that checkpoint refresh is still a
manual admin step, not yet automated.

Also fixes stale deployed-contract info the docs site had drifted on
(ShieldedVault's address and deploy block both predated the WrappedBTC
redeploy).

fix: propagate checkpoint refreshes to already-registered deposit records

Each deposit record freezes checkpointHeight at registration time, and
depositWatcher.ts's own known-txid check skipped calling back into the
one code path (store.createRecord's resubmission branch) that could
have refreshed it — so a checkpoint refresh run after a deposit was
already self-registered would never reach it, confirmed live against
the real deployment: a checkpoint refresh targeting a real 8M-sat
deposit's confirming height didn't unblock it because the record was
still pinned to the old checkpoint. store.refreshCheckpointHeight now
keeps every pending record's checkpointHeight in sync with the live
checkpoint on every watcher poll.

feat: self-register deposits that never reached POST /submit

Closes the mid-flight tab-close gap in the auto-deposit flow: if a
browser closes between broadcasting the deposit tx and reporting its
txid to this backend, the BTC has already moved but nothing would ever
learn about it. A new poll loop independently scans the vault's own
deposit address and self-registers anything template-matching it
doesn't already know, mirroring how btc-withdrawal/watcher.ts already
closes the equivalent gap on the payout side.

feat: auto-broadcast BTC deposit tx when a confirmed UTXO is detected

No behavior change to key custody — the signet signing key still stays
client-side, only the button click is removed. Falls back to a manual
retry button if the automatic attempt fails.
feat: add persisted balance visibility toggles
fix: switch signet faucet link to faucet.coinbin.org

perf: enable cross-origin isolation for multi-threaded WASM proving

@aztec/bb.js's UltraHonk backend silently falls back to single-threaded
WASM without SharedArrayBuffer, which requires COOP/COEP headers this app
never set. Every client-side-proven action (withdraw/pay/placeOrder/
cancelOrder/matchOrders) was paying that cost on every proof. Using
COEP "credentialless" rather than "require-corp" since the WalletConnect
connector's own QR modal loads cross-origin assets that don't send
Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy headers — verified crossOriginIsolated is
true and nothing else broke (faucet/shield/portfolio/pay/swap, no new
console errors).

feat: rebuild BTC bridge to mint real public WrappedBTC, not a private note

Deposits used to mint a hidden Poseidon2 note directly into the shielded
pool, with no real EVM-side collateral and a manual on-chain "claim" step —
so a deposited BTC never had a public balance to shield from, and
withdraw() could never legitimately pay it back out.

btc_deposit's circuit now binds the depositor's own EVM address (extracted
from the deposit tx's OP_RETURN output) and amount as public outputs
instead. depositExternal mints real WrappedBTC (new ERC20, 8 decimals)
straight to that address; from there it's ordinary allowlisted collateral —
shield/withdraw/pay/dark-pool all work on it exactly like FXRP/USDT0, with
no BTC-specific branching. A new backend poll loop (btc-deposit/minter.ts)
submits the mint automatically once a deposit is proven, closing the
manual-claim gap entirely.

Redeployed ShieldedVault + BtcDepositHonkVerifier + WrappedBTC to Coston2
(reusing the five unchanged verifiers and other registries), registered a
fresh checkpoint, redeployed the proving Lambda, and folded the old
/deposit-btc page into the Faucet page (auto-derived signet address, one-
click build/sign/broadcast) and Shield's now-generic deposit form.
feat: implement responsive marketing landing page with hero section and feature cards

feat: wire BTC into Portfolio/Shield/Pay/Swap, redeploy vault

Frontend: BTC (assetId 999) is now a real 4th option everywhere the
other three assets already were — same row, grid-cols-3 to
grid-cols-4, not a separate section. Portfolio skips its public
balanceOf/getBalance query for it (no EVM balance exists for an
external-source asset — added ChainDeployment.external for this).
Shield's combined deposit/withdraw page disables the Deposit action
for BTC with a redirect to the dedicated /deposit-btc flow (shield()
would revert — BTC is only ever minted via depositExternal), but
Withdraw works as-is; its destination field now accepts a pasted
bech32 signet address (tb1q...) and decodes it to the hash160 hex
withdraw() expects, skips compliance screening entirely for external
assets (the contract already does), and no longer yanks the typed
text out from under the user once it becomes a decodable address
(input showed the derived value instead of what was typed). Pay and
Swap needed no balance-query changes — both already operate purely on
local shielded notes, and Swap's placeOrder/matchOrders never had an
asset allowlist at the contract level.

Pay itself needed a contract fix to actually work: redeployed
ShieldedVault (0x46283cc9C4946290c352a064fd6503900F8f027b) with pay()
now exempting isExternalSourceAsset from its isAllowedAsset check,
mirroring withdraw()'s existing branch. No circuit/verifier changed,
so this reuses all 6 existing verifiers. Checkpoint re-registered on
the new vault.

fix: exempt external-source assets from pay()'s isAllowedAsset check

BTC (isExternalSourceAsset) was never added to isAllowedAsset — only
depositExternal mints it, shield() correctly never touches it — but
pay() required isAllowedAsset unconditionally, so a BTC-backed note
could be minted and withdrawn but never privately paid to anyone.
Mirrors withdraw()'s own isExternal branch exactly. Two new tests:
pay() succeeds for an external-source asset even with isAllowedAsset
explicitly revoked, and still rejects an asset that's neither.

fix: allow a stuck deposit's checkpointHeight to be refreshed

Discovered live during an actual end-to-end deposit test: checkpointHeight
is captured once at /submit time and never otherwise revisited
(assembleDepositProofInputs trusts whatever the record already has), so
a record submitted while an older checkpoint was live stayed
permanently unprovable even after the checkpoint got refreshed to the
exact value that would have matched its real confirming height — no
existing endpoint could recover it. Same-blinding resubmission (same
legitimate depositor; an attacker can't produce it, see the existing
BlindingMismatchError check right above this) now refreshes the stored
checkpointHeight instead of just returning the stale record as-is —
but only while still awaiting_proof; a proven/failed record is a
terminal result, not something a resubmission should mutate.

fix: add mempool.emzy.de as a third signet data source

blockstream.info's rate limit against Render's IP held for several
minutes during a live end-to-end deposit test, not the seconds a
transient blip would suggest, so two sources still weren't enough.
mempool.emzy.de is a community-run mirror, cross-checked against a
known real block hash before trusting it (serves the same real signet
chain).

fix: real multi-source fallback for signet data fetches

Discovered live during an actual end-to-end deposit test: Render's
network can't reach mempool.space at all (a prior fix already pointed
MEMPOOL_SIGNET_API_BASE at blockstream.info for that reason), and
blockstream.info then rate-limited Render's IP under this session's
own testing traffic — a real deposit's /submit call sat blocked for
several minutes with no automatic recovery, since every signet fetch
in both btc-deposit/mempool.ts and btc-withdrawal/mempool.ts only ever
tried one hardcoded base.

Both files now try mempool.space then blockstream.info in turn (an
explicit MEMPOOL_SIGNET_API_BASE override still means exactly that one
source, no fallback). Also moved the btc-deposit /submit route's own
raw-tx fetch onto this shared, fallback-aware mempoolGet instead of
its own separate single-URL fetch — the earlier MEMPOOL_BASE fix there
only pointed it at blockstream.info specifically, so it had the exact
same single-point-of-failure problem the rest of this commit closes.

feat: client-side signet Bitcoin wallet, no separate wallet needed

Removes the biggest friction point in the BTC deposit flow: previously
a depositor needed their own external signet wallet capable of custom
OP_RETURN transactions, with no guidance on how to get or use one.

btcWallet.ts derives a real secp256k1 signet keypair deterministically
from the same wallet signature keys.ts/privacyKeys.ts already use for
spendingKey/privacyKey (own domain-separated label, no new signature
prompt, no new wallet to create or back up) — same bitcoinjs-lib/
ecpair/tiny-secp256k1 stack backend/src/btc-withdrawal already uses
server-side, run here in the browser. /deposit-btc now defaults to:
derive address -> fund it from a real signet faucet -> pick a UTXO ->
one button builds, signs, and broadcasts the exact fixed-template
transaction, then hands the txid straight into the existing proving
pipeline. The old manual "construct your own transaction" flow is kept
as a collapsed "Advanced" fallback for anyone who wants to use their
own tooling — and its vault-address display now shows the real
deployed pubkey hash instead of the all-zero placeholder it silently
still had.

Verified against the real browser bundle (both `next dev` and a
production `next build && next start`), not just typechecked: a
throwaway route exercised the real WASM/Buffer-polyfill path,
independently re-verified the resulting ECDSA signature the same way
backend/test/btc-withdrawal.test.ts already does for the server-side
signer, confirmed the built transaction's witness-stripped size is
byte-exact (125) against the circuit's fixed template, and confirmed
deterministic re-derivation (same signature -> same address) across
independent page loads. Route deleted after verification.

feat: wire BTC deposit into the frontend nav and faucet page

The /deposit-btc page was fully built and functional but completely
unlinked from the rest of the UI — no navbar entry, no CTA anywhere,
only reachable by typing the URL directly. Added it to the main nav
(navbar.tsx's single navLinks array drives both desktop and mobile),
and added a dedicated Bitcoin Signet card to the faucet page — BTC
doesn't fit the existing EVM-balance-polling REAL_ASSETS pattern there
(different chain, no wagmi balance, a real external signet faucet
instead of Flare's), so it gets its own explanation + two CTAs: claim
real signet BTC, then go build the actual deposit transaction.

Verified with Playwright against a local dev server: nav link renders
and successfully routes to /deposit-btc, faucet card renders with the
correct signetfaucet.com link, zero console errors either page.

fix: three security/correctness bugs in btc-deposit and btc-withdrawal

1. btc-deposit /submit could be front-run: anyone watching the public
   vault address for a confirmed deposit tx could race to submit that
   txid with a garbage blinding before the real depositor's frontend
   did, silently bricking their note (note_commitment would use the
   wrong blinding, unspendable by the real owner). Resubmission with a
   different blinding now throws BlindingMismatchError (409) instead
   of silently returning the existing record.

2. btc-withdrawal's InsufficientFundsError retry was dead: pollOnce
   unconditionally advanced lastProcessedBlock past every scanned
   block regardless of per-event outcome, so a record left `pending`
   after underfunding could never be re-surfaced by the forward-only
   log scan. store.listPending() existed but was never called outside
   its own test. watcher.ts now retries every stored pending record
   directly each poll, independent of block-range scanning.

3. The withdrawal poll loop had no overlap guard: setInterval fires on
   a fixed schedule regardless of whether the previous tick's promise
   resolved, and fulfillOne only skipped records already `broadcast`
   (not `pending`) — a slow cycle could let two overlapping polls both
   sign and broadcast a payout for the same nullifierHash. Added a
   running-flag guard that skips a tick if the previous one is still
   in flight.

Also gitignored btc-deposit-worker/lambda-build and function.zip
(Lambda deploy build artifacts, currently unignored).

fix: set BTC_VAULT_PUBKEY_HASH in backend CI

Without it, mempool.ts falls back to a zero placeholder in CI (no
backend/.env there, correctly gitignored), diverging from
btc-deposit.test.ts's hardcoded real-address expectation and failing
the build job — which also blocks this workflow's own Render deploy
step. Not a secret, so it's a plain workflow env var, not a repo secret.

fix: use singular rate unit for 1-minute EventBridge schedule

AWS rejects rate(1 minutes) with a ValidationException — it requires
the singular form at exactly 1 (rate(1 minute)). Caught on first real
deploy; POLL_MINUTES defaults to 1 here so this isn't an edge case.

fix: honor MEMPOOL_SIGNET_API_BASE in btc-deposit /submit route

Discovered live on Render: mempool.space is unreachable from Render's
network specifically (reachable everywhere else tested), and this route
had a hardcoded mempool.space URL that ignored the env var override
already used everywhere else in mempool.ts, so switching the deployed
override to blockstream.info didn't fix this one route.
Merge branch 'btc-deposit'

feat: add real BTC signet deposit/withdrawal bridge

Adds a full one-way BTC deposit path (Noir/Barretenberg header-chain +
Merkle-inclusion circuit, depositExternal on ShieldedVault, mempool.space
data-sourcing backend, standalone proving worker with AWS Lambda
deployment) and a BTC withdrawal path (custodial relayer over the
existing withdraw circuit, Turso-backed durable store, solvency
endpoint). Redeploys ShieldedVault (ExternalDeposit/checkpoints/
isExternalSourceAsset) and a new BtcDepositHonkVerifier to Coston2,
reusing the five unchanged verifiers. Registers the initial BTC
checkpoint on-chain.
Fix typo in project name from 'UBRA' to 'UMBRA'

commit.message: fix(wallet-modal): dedupe on resolved label to drop iconless second Rabby entry

fix: harden submission — honest FDC status, relayer limits, CI coverage, lint

Ships the review punch list from the last audit pass:

- README: correct the FDC compliance claim to match ComplianceRegistry's
  actual ATTESTER_ROLE placeholder, add DoraHacks submission fields
  (target user, tracks, newly-built statement), add a Roadmap section.
- Relayer: rate-limit /api/relayer/relay by IP, scope CORS to real origins
  instead of wide-open. (Skipped the proof-length check — bb's generated
  verifiers already do this before any expensive verification runs.)
- CI: add contracts (local Hardhat network) and frontend (lint/typecheck/
  build) workflows; enable backend's real test suite in CI via per-test
  it.skipIf(process.env.CI) guards on the handful of tests that need a
  funded key (compliance, dark-engine, relayer), rather than excluding
  those files wholesale — verified with secrets fully removed.
- Frontend: fix all 5 lint errors (incl. correcting a comment that wrongly
  claimed one React rule couldn't be suppressed) and vendor both fonts
  locally instead of fetching from Google at build time.
- PrivacyKeyRegistry: enforce the documented 33-byte key length on-chain;
  redeployed to Coston2 (0x8107172F8078c965bC9F334fD0bFefB2cFFAe275) and
  rewired everywhere since the prior instance was already live.

feat: encrypt StealthAnnouncer metadata, add stealth-tagged pay() addresses

announce() metadata (amount/asset/blinding) was plaintext ABI-encoded bytes,
and pay()'s stealthAddress was the recipient's real wallet address -
contradicting the "what stays private" table for both dark pool orders and
private pay. Closes both gaps: metadata is now ECIES-encrypted (secp256k1
ECDH + AEAD) to a key each wallet publishes once via the new
PrivacyKeyRegistry contract, and pay() announcements derive a one-time
stealthAddress from that same key instead of publishing the recipient's real
address. Falls back to the legacy plaintext/real-address form for a
counterparty who hasn't registered yet, so nothing already on-chain breaks.

PrivacyKeyRegistry deployed to Coston2 at
0xCE49ab341F1E578Cc86264E83e9dbb6ACD3d6d5A and wired into both
coston2Addresses.json and coston2Deployment.json.

feat: deploy BatchWithdrawer, cap Unshield All at 1 signature

"Unshield All" called withdraw() once per note — N notes meant N separate
wallet signatures, unbounded by anything. Adds BatchWithdrawer, a small
permissionless call-forwarder deployed to Coston2
(0x4E90ECc46d47FF8B8a13F5396931838b256A3fC1): every note's withdraw proof
is still generated locally (no signature needed for that), but submission
now goes through one batched transaction instead of one per note. Holds no
funds — each withdraw() still pays its own recipient directly — and needs
no constructor wiring, since it takes the vault address as a call-time
parameter rather than baking it in. Each item is try/catch'd individually
so one failing withdrawal (a stale root, an already-spent nullifier)
doesn't block the rest, preserving the existing partial-success UX.

Covered by 3 tests using the same real Noir/UltraHonk fixture proof the
existing ShieldedVault tests use — a real batched withdrawal, a failing
item not blocking a valid one in the same batch, and confirming the
contract never holds funds. Full suite (16 tests) still passes.

Frontend falls back to the old one-signature-per-note behavior if
deployment.batchWithdrawer is unset for a given chain.

feat: persist notification bell history across page reloads

The bell's "System Signals" list lived in plain React state — a reload
silently wiped your whole recent-activity history. Persists to
localStorage now, same pattern already used for the isEntered flag: loaded
client-only after mount (not a lazy useState initializer) to avoid an SSR
hydration mismatch, since localStorage doesn't exist server-side.

Deliberately browser-local only, not synced anywhere further — see the
cross-device discussion this followed. A server-side store for this would
mean a backend learning wallet activity, including payment amounts that
today never touch any backend at all.

Verified via Playwright: a real notification survives an actual page
reload and still shows in the bell dropdown afterward.

docs: document order/refund self-announcement in the swap guide

Placing an order and cancelling one both now involve a second on-chain
confirmation (see the matching backend/frontend commit) — update the step
table and the public-disclosure claims to match, instead of leaving the
docs describing the old single-tx behavior.

feat: self-announce placed orders and cancel-order refunds for cross-device recovery

Every note this app creates for someone else (a payment, matched dark-pool
proceeds, a residual order) already goes through StealthAnnouncer, which
means any device holding the right wallet signature can recover it by
scanning the chain — no server, no export file needed. The two exceptions
were notes a trader creates for themselves with no announcement step at
all: a freshly-placed order's own commitment, and a cancel-order refund.
Both used random (non-deterministic) blinding and were saved only to this
browser's local IndexedDB — lose that, lose the note, permanently, with
no recovery path (unlike deposit notes, which use deterministic blinding
specifically so they can be recovered).

Closes that gap by self-announcing both to the trader's own wallet address,
the same way a payment or matched-proceeds note already is. A different
device can now find and claim them via the existing Incoming/My-Orders
claim flow. Best-effort and non-fatal: the order/refund is already valid
on-chain either way, so a failed self-announce doesn't roll anything back
or surface as an error — it just means that device stays the sole copy
until it re-syncs.

Tradeoff worth being explicit about: this adds a second on-chain tx (and
wallet prompt) to placing or cancelling an order, and a small new metadata
link — an announcement to your own address at the same block as the
OrderPlaced/OrderCancelled event, which today reveals nothing about who's
involved. Same shape of tradeoff the pay flow already accepted for its own
announce step.

Also adds encodeOrderMetadata to the frontend's announcer.ts — encoding an
order for announcement previously only existed backend-side (the matcher
announcing a residual after a partial fill).

feat: rework notification system for actual user visibility

Four fixes to how the app surfaces feedback:

1. Clean error messages. A rejected/reverted wallet call was dumping viem's
   full err.message into the notification — the entire request calldata,
   tens of thousands of hex characters, meant for a dev console. Added
   getErrorMessage() (utils.ts), which prefers viem's own shortMessage
   ("User rejected the request.") and hard-caps any fallback. Applied at
   every catch block across swap/pay/shield.

2. Real-time toasts, not just a bell badge. Every notification previously
   only appended to a dropdown behind the bell icon with a small dot — miss
   the bell, miss the event entirely (that's how a stale-order duplicate
   match failure went unnoticed earlier in this session). Added a
   NotificationToastStack, mounted globally, that pops every notification
   as an auto-dismissing toast (errors/warnings stay up longer) while still
   logging to the bell history. The faucet's existing asset-themed toast
   opts out via a new skipToast param so the two don't stack.

3. Type-coded icons. The bell dropdown rendered every entry identically
   regardless of success/error/warning/info — now each gets a matching
   icon+color, same mapping as the new toast.

4. Explorer links + specific amounts. Notifications for on-chain actions
   (place/cancel order, shield, withdraw, pay, register) now carry the tx
   hash for a "View on Explorer" link, and messages that used to say
   "Order Placed" now say what and how much ("Selling 10 FXRP for at least
   9 C2FLR").

Also fixed a duplicate "Wallet Connected" notification — it fired once from
WalletModal's onSuccess callback and again from app-provider's own
isConnected/address effect, both for the same connection.

Verified via Playwright against a local dev build: a real "Secure Vault
Session" notification correctly showed a green success icon in both the
bell dropdown and the new toast simultaneously, no console errors.

fix: dedupe incoming note/order claims against all known notes, not just unspent ones

scanIncomingNotes and scanIncomingOrders both filtered "already claimed"
candidates against getUnspentNotesForWallet — but a claimed note/order that
later gets spent (paid onward, matched, cancelled) drops out of that set
while its announcement stays in StealthAnnouncer's event log forever. The
next scan would offer it as claimable again, and claiming it a second time
collided with the note store's commitment uniqueness index:
"Unable to add key to index 'byCommitment': at least one key does not
satisfy the uniqueness requirements."

Dedupes against every locally-known note regardless of spent status instead.

docs: add tech-stack badges and architecture diagram to README

Adds a Mermaid architecture diagram (validated by rendering it with
mermaid-cli before committing) showing how the frontend, backend modules,
matcher-worker Lambda, Turso store, and Coston2 contracts actually connect,
plus a tech-stack badge row alongside the existing CI/docs/license badges.

docs: modernize README, add MIT license

Restructures the README into a clearer, more scannable format (contents
nav, quick start up top, real CI/docs/license badges) without changing any
of the factual content already corrected in prior commits.

Adds LICENSE (MIT, Hacknest Team / Web3Nova).

chore(docs): bump version to verify Vercel deploys after disabling requireVerifiedCommits

No content change — this commit exists purely to confirm the docs site
actually deploys now that the team-level requireVerifiedCommits policy
(which was silently canceling every deployment since Aug 3rd) is off.

docs: fix stale README and remove orphaned Receive guide

README described an earlier vision of the project (TEE/Google Cloud
Confidential Space matching, Circom, an empty contract/ placeholder,
"simulated" backend behavior, a stale frontend page list) that no longer
matches the real, working implementation — off-chain matcher with
proof-authorized settlement, deployed Coston2 contracts, real FTSOv2/relayer/
compliance calls, and no standalone /receive page (that functionality moved
into Pay's Incoming tab and Swap's My Orders tab a while back).

Removes docs/content/guides/receive.mdx, which documented that now-removed
page, and folds its content (publishing a payment key, claiming incoming
payments) into pay.mdx where the real functionality now lives. Updates every
cross-reference to the old page across the docs site.

chore: remove dead WebAuthn stub and other unused code

WebAuthn/passkey auth was never real (no credential verification, just a
random-hex challenge in a Set) and never called by the frontend, which
authenticates purely via wallet-connect. Removes the module, its route
mount, test, OpenAPI docs, and the cosmetic landing-page badge.

Also removes other confirmed-unused code found in the same sweep: four
orphaned frontend components (liquid-glass-button, dock, mouse-glow,
sidebar), the zod/react-hook-form deps nothing imports, two dead backend
exports (getOperatorAddress, assetBySymbol), a dead frontend note-store
getter (getNoteByCommitment), and a stale file-tree.txt plus doc references
to modules that no longer exist.

fix: persist dark-engine order book/matches, reject stale already-settled orders

Render's free web-service plan has no persistent disk and spins down on
idle, wiping the matcher's in-memory order book and match records on every
restart. That's why matches were rare (both sides need to be resting in the
same live process to ever pair up) and why NullifierAlreadySpent failures
kept recurring (a resubmit of an order already matched+settled in a
since-forgotten process looked brand new and formed a doomed duplicate).

Adds a Turso-backed durable store that every book/match mutation writes
through to, rehydrated on boot before the server accepts traffic. Also
checks isSpentNullifier on-chain before ever (re)matching an order, so a
stale resubmit is rejected outright instead of reverting on-chain.

feat: live-rate context on pending orders, best-price toggle, network activity feed

Three UX gaps in Dark Swap: a resting order gave no indication of why it
hadn't matched, placing an order always required picking a limit price
manually, and there was no feedback anywhere that matching actually works
(only your own balance quietly changing on Portfolio proved it).

- Each order in "My Orders" now shows its own live-rate comparison ("12%
  above market — this is likely why it hasn't matched") via a new OrderRow
  component, plus how long it's been resting.
- Place Order defaults to a "Best available price" toggle — fills at a
  shade under the live rate with no pricing decision required at all;
  switching it off reveals the existing manual-minimum input.
- The timeline panel shows a network-wide "Recent Matches" feed (commitments
  never exposed, same privacy boundary as the rest of this matcher) while
  idle, replacing the static "Awaiting execution" placeholder with actual
  proof that settlement happens.

fix: dedup order submission, mark unsettleable matches as failed instead of retrying forever

Found after the CRS_PATH fix let proving actually run for the first time:
4 of 5 stuck matches all referenced the same nullifier hash — the same
order had been submitted to the matcher more than once (almost certainly
via repeatedly clicking "Resubmit" on an order that looked dropped but was
actually already matched and correctly removed from the book), producing
duplicate matches for one underlying order. Whichever settled first
permanently spent that nullifier; the rest could only ever revert with
NullifierAlreadySpent, forever, on every 5-minute poll.

Two fixes:
- submitOrder now checks a commitment-to-match index and the resting book
  before attempting a fresh match, so a duplicate submission of an
  already-matched or already-resting order is a no-op instead of a new
  doomed match.
- settleOnChain recognizes a NullifierAlreadySpent revert specifically and
  marks the match "failed" (a new terminal status) rather than leaving it
  "awaiting_proof" — the matcher-worker only polls for awaiting_proof, so a
  failed match stops being retried instead of wasting a proving run every
  cycle indefinitely. completeMatch/submitExternalProof only announce on an
  actual settlement now, since a failed match has nothing that was really
  inserted on-chain to announce.

fix: set CRS_PATH so matcher-worker's proving actually works on Lambda

Every match settlement attempt was failing identically: bb.js caches its
reference string at homedir()/.bb-crs by default, which Lambda's read-only
filesystem rejects outright. Confirmed by reading bb.js's own source that
it respects CRS_PATH — set to /tmp, the one writable path in a Lambda
execution environment. Applied directly to the live function and captured
here so future deploys keep it. Verified against production: a real proof
now generates and a real match settled on-chain that previously couldn't
get past the filesystem error at all.

feat(pay): track incoming payments through the execution timeline

The Incoming tab left the timeline panel showing "awaiting execution" no
matter what was happening, so a payment arriving and being claimed produced
no visible progress. It now runs its own four-step track: announced,
ownership verified, claim in flight, spendable.

Announce and verify resolve together because scanIncomingNotes discards any
candidate whose commitment doesn't recompute against our ownerKey, so nothing
unverified can reach the list.

Consolidates the asset formatting fixed in 68c13df into one describeAmount
helper, since the timeline needs the same symbol and decimal lookup.

feat: restore residual-order claiming, live-rate hint on Swap, fix asset display bug

The now-deleted /receive page was the only place that ever claimed a
partial fill's residual order (scanIncomingOrders/claimIncomingOrder) —
that functionality had nowhere left to live. Added it to the Swap page's
"My Orders" tab instead: unclaimed residuals show above the open-orders
list with a Claim button.

Also on Swap: an order priced far from the live market rate (e.g. asking
for double the real rate) silently never fills, with no indication why.
The "Minimum Acceptable Amount" field now shows the live FTSOv2 rate and
how far the entered value sits from it, and defaults to a value 1% under
the live rate (still fully editable) so a first attempt is actually
fillable instead of guessed blind.

Pay's Incoming list showed "(asset 0)" instead of a token symbol, and
hardcoded 18 decimals regardless of the real asset — meaning a claimed
FXRP/USDT0 payment (6 decimals) would display a wildly wrong amount, not
just a missing label. Now resolves both from the deployment config.

feat(faucet): center the receipt toast with a per-asset traveling highlight

Moves the toast to the viewport center and drops the green-tinted card for a
neutral graphite one, so the only colour is the asset's own: a conic beam that
sweeps the border ring in red for C2FLR, green for USDT0, black for FXRP.

Also removes the /receive page and its nav and sidebar entries.

fix: paginate incoming-payment scans, check tx status on backend, add order resubmit

Incoming payments and residual orders were undiscoverable for everyone:
fetchIncomingAnnouncements/fetchIncomingOrderAnnouncements did one unbounded
eth_getLogs call from the vault's deploy block to latest, which now exceeds
drpc.org's 10,000-block cap and fails outright. Extracted the existing
chunking fix (from the deposit scanner) into a shared getLogsChunked helper
and applied it here too.

Backend had the same missing-receipt-status-check bug as the frontend, but
worse: submitMatch/announceMatchedNote/announceResidualOrder never checked
waitForTransactionReceipt's status, so a reverted matchOrders() call could
still get marked "settled" and announce a match to both traders that was
never actually inserted on-chain, while silently dropping a still-valid
order from the matcher's book. Added assertTxSuccess (mirroring the
frontend one) and applied it across submitter.ts, the compliance screening
endpoint, and the relayer service. Also distinguished a genuine on-chain
failure from the routine "no prover configured" case in the matcher's logs,
so the former doesn't get buried as if it were expected.

Added a "Resubmit to Matcher" action on the Swap page: the order book is
in-memory on the backend with no persistence, so an order can silently fall
out of it (backend restart/redeploy, or the matcher being unreachable at
submission time) while staying fully valid and unspent on-chain. Each open
order now shows whether it's confirmed live on the matcher's book, or a
button to hand its details over again.

ci: have the workflow trigger the Render deploy itself, not just watch for one

Render's GitHub-push auto-deploy for this service turned out to be
disconnected — confirmed by hand that every deploy so far was manual/
API-triggered, never from a push webhook, so the prior version of this
job (which only polled for a deploy Render was supposed to start on its
own) timed out every time with nothing to find.

Now the workflow calls Render's trigger-deploy API itself and polls that
specific deploy id to completion. If the GitHub connection ever gets
reconnected in Render's dashboard, both would fire per push — redundant
but harmless.

ci: drop npm test from backend CI gate

The backend's test suite submits real Coston2 transactions using a funded
operator key, so it needs PRIVATE_KEY to run at all. Wiring that key into
CI would make it reachable by every push/PR — deliberately not doing that.
CI now only builds/typechecks; npm test stays a local/manual check.

ci: add backend CI/CD workflow with Render deploy verification

Builds and tests the backend on every push/PR touching it, then — for
pushes to main — polls Render's API for the deploy that commit triggers
and fails the check if it doesn't come back live. Render's own GitHub
integration still does the actual deploying; this only reports whether
it worked, since Render doesn't post that back to GitHub the way Vercel
does for the frontend.

Needs RENDER_API_KEY and RENDER_SERVICE_ID as repo secrets (now set).

feat: auto-add Flare networks on switch, wire compliance screening into withdraw

Switching networks now passes addEthereumChainParameter, so a wallet that
doesn't have Coston2 or Flare Mainnet configured yet gets it added instead
of the switch just failing. Applied to the navbar's network switcher and
every page's "switch to Coston2" prompt (shield, pay, swap).

Also: ShieldedVault.withdraw() gates on ComplianceRegistry.isScreened, but
nothing in the UI called the backend's screening endpoint. Withdraw and
Unshield All now check on-chain screening status first and screen the
destination automatically if needed, with a visible status badge and a
new step in the withdraw timeline, before attempting the transaction.

feat: toast when faucet tokens land

The faucet page already watched for the balance to rise after opening
Flare's faucet, but only logged it to the navbar bell, which is easy
to miss. Adds a green glass toast that springs in top-centre and
auto-dismisses after 4s, and states the amount received per asset.

fix: check tx receipt status, attempt real wallet revoke on disconnect

waitForTransactionReceipt resolves even on a reverted transaction — several
flows (withdraw/Unshield All, approve, key registration, pay announcement)
never checked receipt.status and reported success regardless. Added a shared
assertTxSuccess check at every unguarded call site.

Also: injected wallets never actually let go on Disconnect, since wagmi's own
wallet_revokePermissions attempt uses a 100ms timeout too tight to complete.
Now issue that call directly with room to finish before tearing down local
state.

docs: align branding with the landing page

Header reads UMBRA, tab title is Umbra Docs, and the navbar wordmark
now matches the frontend UmbraLogo: same logo.png asset, Space Grotesk
700, wide tracking. Drops the accent dot in favour of "Docs" and
removes the now-unreferenced logo.svg.

fix: point docs links at the live docs site

The nav pill, hero button, and footer all linked to
docs.umbraprotocol.io, which was never registered and returned
nothing. The docs now exist at docs-umbra.vercel.app.

docs: add Nextra documentation site

New top-level docs/ package (Nextra 4.6.1, Next 16.2.12), served
separately from frontend/ so the theme's Tailwind v4 stylesheet and
root layout don't collide with the app's own. The three existing
docs.umbraprotocol.io links already point where this deploys, so no
frontend file changes.

14 pages across Introduction, Getting Started, Concepts, Guides and
Reference. Written from contract/circuits/DESIGN.md, the Noir main()
signatures, the Solidity contracts and the live frontend pages --
deliberately not from README.md, which still carries the TEE/SGX
matching claims removed in def7cfc.

Pins zod to 4.3.6: nextra-theme-docs 4.6.1 destructures `children`
out of props before LayoutPropsSchema.safeParse(), but its schema
declares `children: z.custom()`, and zod 4.4.0 made z.custom() reject
undefined. Without the pin every page 500s. Drop once fixed upstream.

feat: cross-device deposit recovery, Unshield All, persisted signing key

- Deposit notes now use deterministic, recoverable blinding (assetId,
  amount, and a per-pair sequential salt) instead of an opaque local index.
  A shield deposit's amount is already public the moment it lands on-chain,
  so a fresh browser/device can now recover its own past deposits by
  scanning Shielded events and searching salts until one matches — no
  export/import step needed. Cancel-order refunds and claimed notes are
  unaffected (their amounts aren't public, so they stay index-blinded, same
  as before). Wired into Shield via a new "Recover Deposits" action.

- Added "Unshield All" on the Withdraw tab: withdraws every note for the
  selected asset in one action instead of one at a time. Still no
  custom-amount partial withdraw — that needs a new circuit (1-in/2-out with
  a change output), out of scope here.

- The wallet-derivation signature is now persisted per-address in
  localStorage instead of memory-only. It never authorizes a transaction by
  itself, and now that a vault session survives a reload too, re-prompting
  on every reload was pure friction with no remaining security upside.

Also reworded a handful of code comments that referenced another project by
name — same technical rationale, no attribution.

fix: withdraw proving, stuck timelines, lost sessions, dead network switcher

- withdraw.json (frontend/public/circuits/) was a stale compiled artifact
  from before the owner_key note scheme rename, still expecting inputs named
  secret/nullifier instead of spending_key/blinding. Every withdraw attempt
  failed with "Expected argument `nullifier`, but none was found" as a
  result. Re-synced from contract/circuits/noir/withdraw/target/withdraw.json,
  the actual current artifact (pay/place_order/cancel_order were already
  in sync, only withdraw had drifted).

- Shield/Pay/Swap execution timelines never showed their final step as
  "Completed", even after the flow genuinely succeeded (currentStepIdx is
  never > its own index) — looked identical to a stuck/failed settlement.

- isEntered was plain React state with no persistence, so any page reload
  dropped the user back at the landing gate mid-session. Now persisted to
  localStorage, restored client-side after mount.

- Navbar's network dropdown was local UI state never wired to wagmi —
  selecting an option didn't switch anything. Now reflects the real
  connected chain and calls switchChain for real; dropped "Songbird
  Network", which was never a configured chain to begin with.

fix: paginate eth_getLogs so full leaf scans don't exceed the free-tier block-range cap

fetchAllLeaves (backend and frontend) fetched the vault's entire leaf
history in one unbounded fromBlock=deployBlock..latest call. That was fine
right after deployment, but the chain has since grown past drpc.org's free
tier cap of 10,000 blocks per eth_getLogs call, so every full scan started
failing with "ranges over 10000 blocks are not supported on free plan" —
breaking dark-pool matching on the backend and Merkle-proof-dependent flows
(withdraw, pay, place/cancel order) on the frontend.

Both scan.ts now resolve "latest" once via getBlockNumber() and fetch in
<=9999-block windows, concatenating results. Confirmed fixed against real
Coston2 state: the dark-engine match test, which was failing with exactly
this RPC error, now passes.

feat: add detailed request and business-logic logging to the backend

Render's logs previously only showed a single boot line — no per-request
logging, and errors caught by the global handler were sent to the client but
never printed anywhere. Adds a shared pino logger (plain human-readable
lines, since Render's dashboard is a plain log viewer, not a JSON pipeline)
wired into every request via pino-http, plus targeted logs at every real
decision point: order submission/resting/matching, proof generation and
on-chain settlement, announcement delivery, relayed transactions, compliance
screening, and FTSO feed reads, so a failure at any step is traceable to
exactly what happened and why instead of a bare error response.

fix: confirm before wallet disconnect, restore button/input legibility

Disconnecting was a one-click irreversible action reachable from three
places, one of which bypassed the provider and fired no notification. All
three now route through a single confirm modal and return to the gateway
so the next connect starts a clean session.

Also: the secondary button variant rendered white-on-white (accent-secondary
and text-primary are both #FFFFFF), token symbols overlapped the amount
inputs on the swap and shield pages, the landing footer CTA now reflects
connection state, and the portfolio balances table shows real token icons
instead of two-letter text badges.

fix: correct inaccurate TEE/SGX matching claims in landing copy

The landing page's hero, "how it works" step, and tech stack grid described
order matching as happening inside Intel SGX / TEE enclaves — that's not
what this stack does. Real matching is off-chain in the backend's
dark-engine, proven correct by the matcher-worker's Noir match_orders
circuit (deployed on Lambda) and verified on-chain, no TEE anywhere.
Reworded to describe the actual zero-knowledge-proven matching flow, and
fixed a matching "Sanitized TEE connection established" notification text
in app-provider. Aspirational stat numbers (TVL, stealth set count, etc.)
left untouched per explicit instruction — only the technical claims changed.

fix: remove fake dashboard shown after Initialize, redirect to real app

Pressing "Initialize"/"Launch App" on the landing page used to swap in a
decorative "Umbra Core" panel on the same "/" route (no distinct URL) with
hardcoded fake stats, a setTimeout-driven ZK proof animation with a made-up
witness/proof/tx hash, and an inaccurate architecture description — none of
it wired to the real vault, notes, or proving code the actual app pages use.

Entering the vault now routes straight to /portfolio, the real entry point
into the app's functional pages. Landing page is otherwise unchanged.

feat: live balance tracking on faucet page instead of manual refresh

Each faucet card now polls the wallet's real balance (native getBalance for
C2FLR, ERC20 balanceOf for FXRP/USDT0) every 5s and refetches immediately on
window focus, so tabbing back after minting on Flare's faucet reflects the
new balance without a manual portfolio check. Clicking "Open Faucet" snapshots
the current balance and watches for it to rise, flashing a success
notification once it does.

feat: hold C2FLR natively in ShieldedVault, remove wrapped-token dependency

shield()/withdraw() now branch on the native asset (assetId 0) and hold/pay
C2FLR directly via msg.value/call, instead of requiring users to wrap into a
separate ERC20 first. The app never exposed a wrap button, so shielded
balances for that token silently never reflected faucet-collected C2FLR.

No circuit or verifier changes needed (assetId/amount are opaque Field
values), so the vault-only redeploy reuses all 5 existing verifiers. Updated
frontend (shield/pay/swap/portfolio) to branch native balance/deposit flow
vs ERC20, fixed portfolio's balance read for the native asset, and swept
remaining references to the old wrapped-token naming across contract,
backend, and docs.

feat: fix pay's unconstrained output, add matchOrders partial fills, AWS Lambda matcher-worker

- pay(): out_commitment is now actually constrained to the spent note's
  real value in-circuit (was a self-referential tautology that let anyone
  spend a trivial note and mint an arbitrary output note)
- matchOrders now supports real partial fills: orders move onto the same
  owner_key(spending_key) scheme notes already use, so a matcher-created
  residual order is spendable by its original trader without the matcher
  choosing anything on their behalf. Fill amounts are proven with pro-rata
  minimum checks (100-bit range bound, widened from an initial 64-bit
  bound that turned out too tight for 18-decimal WFLR amounts — caught by
  a real end-to-end matcher-worker run, not a toy-number unit test)
- backend: fillSizing.ts sizes fills off live FTSOv2 rates and re-verifies
  its own proposal with exact integer math before ever proving; settled
  matches auto-relist any residual onto the book immediately
- matcher-worker is a new standalone package (kept off backend's
  constrained host) that proves match_orders; can now run on AWS Lambda
  on an EventBridge schedule instead of needing an always-on process
- frontend: swap page shows fill progress on partially-filled orders;
  receive page discovers residual orders the same way it already
  discovers payments
- redeployed ShieldedVault + the three order verifiers to Coston2
  (targeted redeploy, reusing the unchanged withdraw/pay verifiers and
  ComplianceRegistry/StealthAnnouncer/OwnerKeyRegistry)

Merge origin/main: landing/nav/branding refresh + backend swagger docs

Resolved conflicts:
- backend/package.json, package-lock.json: keep both viem (dark-engine/
  relayer/compliance) and swagger-ui-express (new /docs endpoint);
  regenerated the lock file via npm install.
- backend/src/app.ts: kept the swagger /docs mount, dropped the vault/
  portfolio routers (those modules were deleted this session — replaced by
  real dark-engine/pricing/compliance/relayer integrations).
- backend/src/docs/openapi.ts: rewritten to document the real current API
  surface instead of the removed vault/portfolio/stealth/prover/old-swap
  endpoints.
- backend/tsconfig.json: kept the DOM lib addition (needed by ftso.client's
  viem types), dropped the redundant moduleResolution key per upstream's
  own cleanup commit.
- frontend/src/app/faucet/page.tsx: kept the deliberate real-Coston2-faucet
  deep-link (no fake mint simulator), adopted upstream's black-glass visual
  treatment and its non-hotlinked networkIcon() helper.

feat: real Noir dark pool contracts, owner_key note scheme, and live backend

Adds the full ZK dark-pool contract stack (Noir/UltraHonk circuits for
withdraw/pay/placeOrder/cancelOrder/matchOrders, ShieldedVault,
ComplianceRegistry, OwnerKeyRegistry, StealthAnnouncer), deployed live to
Flare Coston2. Notes use a public ownerKey/private spendingKey split so a
note can be built for another wallet without ever exposing spend authority.

Frontend: shield/pay/swap/portfolio/receive pages wired directly to the
live contracts with real in-browser Noir/UltraHonk proving (no backend
proxy). Client-side note wallet (key derivation, IndexedDB store, Merkle
scanning) and payment-key registry/announcement flow for private pay.

Backend: replaces simulated vault/portfolio/stealth/prover modules with
real integrations — FTSOv2 pricing, on-chain compliance screening via
ATTESTER_ROLE, a gasless relayer (proof = authorization, no server-side
proving), and a dark-pool matcher with real order book, real Merkle/
Poseidon2 proof-input assembly, and a pluggable prover (defaults to
unavailable, since this deployment doesn't run proving on its constrained
host) — mirrors the poki-tcg/wraith matcher's disclosed trust model.

commit.message:
Polish landing copy and faucet controls

Ground the tech stack section in what the app actually runs, swap the
generic step icons for ones that read as their action, and lift box
opacity so cards stay legible against the black backdrop. Point the
footer GitHub links at the real repo. Drop USDC from the faucet and
narrow the mint button.
feat: add project branding assets and implement navigation and layout components
tsconfig module resolution removal
Merge branch 'main' of https://github.com/davre001/UMBRA
project structure update
swagger ui endpoint glance
dev dependencies vulnerability fix
project structure update

Fix mobile hero layout, shrink nav buttons, animate stat counters

The hero section is justify-center on min-h-screen, so on narrow
viewports the short content block was centered and left ~228px of dead
space directly under the fixed nav. Top-align on mobile instead and keep
centering from sm up.

Also on mobile: the header overflowed horizontally and clipped the
"Launch App" button mid-word. Responsive padding plus min-w-0/truncate on
the logo group and flex-shrink-0/whitespace-nowrap on the buttons keeps
everything inside a 390px viewport.

Add a CountUp component that animates the landing and dashboard stat
numbers into view. It splits a value like "$84.2M" into prefix, number
and suffix so only the numeric run animates and the formatting survives;
it respects prefers-reduced-motion and renders unparseable values as-is.

Fix the Coinbase wallet icon, which never rendered. CONNECTOR_ICONS and
WALLET_META were keyed coinbaseWallet, but wagmi's connector reports its
id as coinbaseWalletSDK, so the lookup missed and the modal fell back to
a generic glyph. Redraw the mark with its ring restored.

Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main'

fix(faucet): raise black-glass contrast against the black backdrop

The panels sat at bg-black/40 over a pure-black body with the WebGL
background behind it, so only the hairline border was visible. Bump the
shells to bg-black/60 with border-white/15 and an inset top highlight,
and lift the nested token cards to bg-white/[0.07] so they separate from
the shell they sit in.
